questions.question: In which of the following Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) is India on track or maintaining SDG achievement, as per the Sustainable Development Report 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**SDG 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Sustainable Development Report 2025**, India has shown significant progress in **SDG 1**, which stands for **No Poverty**. This goal aims to end poverty in all its forms everywhere by the year **2030**. ***Hence, option 2 is correct.***
 
• India is categorized as being **on track** or **maintaining SDG achievement** for this specific goal, largely due to robust **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)** mechanisms and extensive social safety nets.
 
• While progress varies across other goals, **SDG 1** reflects the impact of schemes like the **PM Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana** and the **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)** in reducing extreme financial vulnerability.
 
• In contrast, **SDG 9** (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure) shows moderate improvement but faces structural challenges in full achievement. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **SDG 13** (Climate Action) and **SDG 14** (Life Below Water) continue to face significant or major challenges, with progress often stagnating due to environmental pressures and global climate shifts. ***Hence, options 3 and 4 are incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**
 
 
• The **SDGs** were adopted by all **United Nations Member States** in **2015** as a universal call to action to end poverty, protect the planet, and ensure peace and prosperity by **2030**.
 
• There are **17 Goals** and **169 Targets** that are integrated and recognize that action in one area will affect outcomes in others.
 
 
 
• **SDG 1 - No Poverty:**
 
 
• This goal targets the **eradication of extreme poverty** for all people everywhere, currently measured as people living on less than **$2.15 a day**.
 
• It also focuses on implementing **social protection systems** and ensuring equal rights to economic resources.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Report (SDR):**
 
 
• The **SDR** is published annually by the **Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)**. It provides a global assessment of countries' progress towards the **SDGs**.
 
• The report includes the **SDG Index** and **Dashboards**, which use a **traffic light system** (Green, Yellow, Orange, Red) to visualize progress and remaining gaps.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog and SDGs in India:**
 
 
• In India, **NITI Aayog** is the nodal agency for monitoring **SDG implementation**. It releases the **SDG India Index**, which ranks **States and Union Territories** based on their performance.
 
• The **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)** released by **NITI Aayog** has previously highlighted that millions of Indians have moved out of multidimensional poverty between **2015-16** and **2019-21**.
 
 
 
• **Other SDGs mentioned:**
 
 
• **SDG 9:** Focuses on building resilient **infrastructure**, promoting inclusive and sustainable industrialization, and fostering **innovation**.
 
• **SDG 13:** Urges immediate action to combat **climate change** and its impacts.
 
• **SDG 14:** Aims to conserve and sustainably use the **oceans**, seas, and marine resources.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: For which novel did David Szalay receive the Booker Prize in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Flesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **David Szalay** is a highly acclaimed **British-Canadian** novelist known for his distinct narrative structure and focus on the mundane yet profound aspects of human life.
 
• In **2025**, his novel titled **Flesh** was awarded the prestigious **Booker Prize**, recognizing it as the best work of long-form fiction published in the **United Kingdom** and **Ireland** that year.
 
• The novel **Flesh** explores intricate themes of physical existence, mortality, and the sensory experiences that define the human condition. It was lauded by the judging panel for its visceral prose and emotional resonance.
 
• Prior to this win, **David Szalay** gained significant international attention when his work **All That Man Is** was shortlisted for the **Booker Prize** in **2016**.
 
• The other options provided, such as **The Sea of Trees**, **Heart Lamp**, and **Last Empire**, are fictional titles or distractors in this context and did not receive the award in **2025**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Flesh.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Booker Prize:**
 
 
• Established in **1969**, it was originally known as the **Booker–McConnell Prize**. It is one of the world's leading literary awards, bringing global recognition to the winning author.
 
• The prize is open to writers of any nationality, provided their novel is written in **English** and published in the **UK** or **Ireland**.
 
• The winner receives a cash prize of **£50,000**, while each of the shortlisted authors receives **£2,500** and a specially bound edition of their book.
 
 
 
• **About David Szalay:**
 
 
• Born in **Montreal**, **Canada**, in **1974**, he moved to the **United Kingdom** during his childhood and was educated at **Oxford University**.
 
• His debut novel, **London and the South-East**, was published in **2008** and won the **Betty Trask Award** and the **Geoffrey Faber Memorial Prize**.
 
• He is celebrated for his "composite novels" or short story cycles that function as a single thematic unit, a technique prominently seen in his **2016** work.
 
 
 
• **Literary Impact:**
 
 
• Winning the **Booker Prize** often results in the "Booker Effect," where the winning title sees a massive increase in **international sales** and **translation rights** deals across the globe.
 
• The selection process involves a panel of five judges, typically consisting of critics, writers, academics, and notable public figures, who read over **150 novels** to decide the winner.

questions.question: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is seeking to collaborate with the European Space Agency (ESA) on which of the following missions to track and study the Apophis asteroid, which is slated to make a close encounter with Earth in 2029?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ramses mission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** has expressed its intent to join the **European Space Agency (ESA)** for the **Ramses mission** to study the asteroid **Apophis**.
 
• **Ramses** stands for **Rapid Apophis Mission for Space Safety**, a specialized mission designed to rendezvous with the asteroid before its close encounter with **Earth** in **2029**.
 
• **ISRO Chairman S. Somanath** officially stated during a workshop on **Planetary Defense** that India is looking to collaborate by potentially providing **scientific instruments** or technical support for the mission.
 
• The mission aims to observe the changes in the asteroid's **physical characteristics** and **orbital trajectory** as it is subjected to the **gravitational pull** of **Earth**.
 
• This collaboration is part of a global effort to enhance **Planetary Defense** capabilities, ensuring that space agencies are prepared for potential **Near-Earth Object (NEO)** impacts in the future.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About Asteroid Apophis:**
 
 
• Scientifically known as **99942 Apophis**, it was first discovered in **2004** and was initially considered a significant threat to **Earth**.
 
• The asteroid is approximately **340 to 375 meters** in diameter, making it larger than nearly **90%** of other near-Earth asteroids.
 
• On **April 13, 2029**, it is expected to pass within **32,000 kilometers** of **Earth’s** surface, which is closer than the orbits of **geostationary satellites**.
 
 
 
• **Other Missions to Apophis:**
 
 
• **NASA** is also participating in the study of this asteroid through its **OSIRIS-APEX** mission (formerly OSIRIS-REx).
 
• While **OSIRIS-APEX** will reach the asteroid shortly after its close flyby, the **ESA-led Ramses mission** aims to be there **before** the encounter to witness the transition.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Scientific Significance:** The flyby is a **once-in-a-millennium** opportunity for scientists to observe how an asteroid's **rotation** and **surface structure** (including potential "asteroid quakes") change due to **tidal forces** from a planet.
 
• **Planetary Defense:** The data gathered from the **Ramses mission** will be crucial for **Planetary Defense** strategies, helping scientists understand how to deflect or mitigate the impact of hazardous asteroids in the future.
 
• **ISRO's Growing Role:** India’s interest in the **Ramses mission** marks a significant expansion of **ISRO's** footprint in **deep-space exploration** and international scientific diplomacy beyond lunar and martian missions.
 
• **ESA's Timeline:** The **ESA** must launch the **Ramses** spacecraft by **early 2028** to ensure it arrives at **Apophis** in time for the **April 2029** event.

questions.question: Which former Olympic swimmer was elected as the first female and African President of the IOC in March 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kirsty Coventry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kirsty Coventry**, a legendary swimmer from **Zimbabwe**, was elected as the **President** of the **International Olympic Committee (IOC)** in **March 2025**.
 
• Her election is a landmark event in sporting history, as she became the **first woman** and the **first individual from the African continent** to lead the organization since its founding in **1894**.
 
• She succeeded **Thomas Bach**, who served as the **IOC President** for **12 years** from **2013 to 2025**.
 
• Coventry is one of the most decorated Olympians in history, having won a total of **7 Olympic medals** (including **2 Gold**, **4 Silver**, and **1 Bronze**) across the **2004 Athens** and **2008 Beijing** Olympic Games.
 
• Before ascending to the presidency, she held significant administrative roles, including serving as **Zimbabwe's Minister of Sport, Arts, and Recreation** and the **Chair of the IOC Athletes' Commission** from **2018 to 2021**.
 
• The election took place during the **143rd IOC Session** held in **Ancient Olympia, Greece**, where she secured the majority of votes against other prominent candidates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **International Olympic Committee (IOC):**
 
 
• The **IOC** is a non-governmental sports organization based in **Lausanne, Switzerland**.
 
• It is the supreme authority of the **Olympic Movement** and is responsible for the supervision and administration of the **Summer** and **Winter Olympic Games**.
 
• The **Olympic Charter** governs the organization, outlining the rules and guidelines for the Games and the conduct of the committee members.
 
 
 
• **Kirsty Coventry’s Athletic Career:**
 
 
• Known as Africa's **"Golden Girl,"** she is the most successful African Olympian in the history of swimming.
 
• She competed in **five consecutive Olympic Games**, starting from **Sydney 2000** to **Rio 2016**.
 
• Her primary events were the **100m and 200m backstroke**, as well as individual medley events.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Overview:**
 
 
• **Penny Heyns:** A former **South African** swimmer who made history at the **1996 Atlanta Olympics** by winning gold in both the **100m and 200m breaststroke**.
 
• **Cathy Freeman:** An **Australian** former sprinter who specialized in the **400 meters** and famously won the gold medal at the **2000 Sydney Olympics**.
 
• **Inge de Bruijn:** A **Dutch** former competitive swimmer and **four-time Olympic champion** who held multiple world records in the early **2000s**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:** Since **1894**, the **IOC** has had **eight presidents**, all of whom were men, and seven of whom were from **Europe** (with the exception of **Avery Brundage** from the **USA**).
 
• **Presidential Term:** Under the current **Olympic Charter**, the president is elected by secret ballot for an initial term of **eight years**, with the possibility of being re-elected for a second term of **four years**.
 
• **Diversity and Inclusion:** Coventry’s presidency is seen as a pivotal shift toward **gender equality** and **global representation** within the highest echelons of international sports governance.
 
• **Vision:** During her campaign, she emphasized **transparency**, the **protection of clean athletes**, and increasing the accessibility of sports in **developing nations**.

questions.question: Who was conferred the Padma Shri in 2025 for revitalising Kani shawl weaving in the field of Art and Literature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Farooq Ahmad Mir**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Farooq Ahmad Mir** has been honored with the **Padma Shri** award in **2025** for his exceptional contribution to the field of **Art**, specifically for his work in revitalizing the traditional **Kani shawl weaving**.
 
• He hails from the **Budgam** district in the Union Territory of **Jammu & Kashmir**, a region renowned for its rich heritage in textile arts.
 
• The **Kani shawl** is one of the oldest and most intricate handicrafts of **Kashmir**, involving a specialized weaving technique that uses small wooden eyeless needles called **‘Kanis’** instead of a traditional shuttle.
 
• **Farooq Ahmad Mir** is credited with preventing this ancient art form from becoming extinct by training hundreds of local artisans and ensuring the preservation of the **Talim** (the coded script used for weaving patterns).
 
• His efforts have not only preserved a cultural legacy but also provided sustainable livelihoods to numerous families in the **Kashmir Valley**, bringing international recognition back to this **Mughal-era** craft.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kani Shawl Weaving:**
 
 
• The word **'Kani'** refers to the small **wooden sticks** made from forest wood that are used to weave the intricate floral and paisley designs.
 
• Unlike other shawls where the design is embroidered after weaving, in **Kani shawls**, the design is woven directly into the fabric using **Pashmina** wool.
 
• A single **Kani shawl** can take anywhere from **six months to two years** to complete, depending on the complexity of the pattern.
 
• The craft was granted a **Geographical Indication (GI) tag** in **2008**, which provides legal protection and ensures the authenticity of shawls produced in the **Kanihama** area of **Jammu & Kashmir**.
 
 
 
• **Padma Awards 2025:**
 
 
• The **Padma Awards** are among the highest civilian honors in **India**, announced annually on the eve of **Republic Day** (**January 26**).
 
• The awards are given in three categories: **Padma Vibhushan** (for exceptional and distinguished service), **Padma Bhushan** (distinguished service of high order), and **Padma Shri** (distinguished service).
 
• The **2025** list includes several "unsung heroes" from across **India** who have made significant impacts in **Art**, **Social Work**, **Literature**, **Science**, and **Sports**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Technical Aspects of the Craft:**
 
 
• The weaving process is guided by the **Talim**, a written code that instructs the weaver on the number of threads and colors to be used for every single stitch.
 
• Historically, these shawls were highly prized by **Mughal Emperors** like **Akbar**, who was a great patron of **Kashmiri** textiles.
 
• The **Pashmina** wool used in these shawls is sourced from the **Changthangi goat** found in the high-altitude regions of **Ladakh**.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Context:**
 
 
• **Bhimavva Doddabalappa Shillekyathara** is often associated with folk arts like **Dollu Kunitha** from **Karnataka**.
 
• **Stephen Knapp** was an **American** artist known for his light paintings (light dispensed through glass), highlighting the international reach of the **Art** category in the **Padma** awards during certain years.
 
 
</ul

• **ENDOVEDA** is an advanced digital platform designed to revolutionize **endoscopy reporting** by making it more efficient, standardized, and data-driven for medical professionals.
 
• The platform was officially unveiled in **July 2025** during **Endocon 2025**, a premier national conference held in **Jaipur**, **Rajasthan**.
 
• The primary objective of **ENDOVEDA** is to automate and streamline the documentation process for **gastrointestinal (GI) procedures**, which historically required significant manual effort and time.
 
• It utilizes **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** and **Natural Language Processing (NLP)** to help **gastroenterologists** generate reports that are accurate and compliant with global medical standards.
 
• The launch at **Endocon 2025** highlights the increasing role of **indigenous MedTech** solutions in improving healthcare delivery within **India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Endocon Conference:**
 
 
• **Endocon** is the flagship annual event of the **Society of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy of India (SGEI)**.
 
• The conference serves as a platform for **doctors**, researchers, and **medical technology** companies to showcase the latest innovations in **minimally invasive surgery** and **diagnostic imaging**.
 
• The **2025 edition** in **Jaipur** focused heavily on "The Future of AI in Endoscopy," aiming to reduce diagnostic errors and improve patient outcomes.

• **Digital Health Integration:**
 
 
• The development of such platforms aligns with the **Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM)**, which aims to create a seamless **digital health ecosystem** across **India**.
 
• By converting procedural findings into structured **digital records**, these platforms facilitate easier sharing of patient history between different healthcare providers.
 
 
 
• **Society of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy of India (SGEI):**
 
 
• Established in **1982**, the **SGEI** is a professional body dedicated to the advancement of **endoscopic practices** in the country.
 
• It plays a vital role in training **young clinicians** and setting the ethical and technical guidelines for **gastroenterology** in **India**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Location:** The choice of **Jaipur** as the venue for **Endocon 2025** underscores the city's growth as a major **medical hub** in **North India**, capable of hosting large-scale **international health conclaves**.
 
• **Technological Features:** **ENDOVEDA** likely features **cloud-based storage**, allowing doctors to access endoscopy videos and reports remotely, which is a significant step toward **tele-medicine**.
 
• **Market Impact:** The introduction of such specialized **software-as-a-service (SaaS)** models in the **Indian healthcare market** is expected to lower the administrative costs for private clinics and government hospitals alike.

questions.question: Which of the following sectors is given special focus under the Employment Linked Incentive (ELI) Scheme launched in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Manufacturing**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Employment Linked Incentive (ELI) Scheme** was a major highlight of the **Union Budget 2024-25**, presented by **Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman**. The scheme is part of the **Prime Minister’s Package for Education, Employment, and Skilling**, with an aim to create **4.1 crore jobs** over five years.
 
• Among the three sub-schemes introduced, **Scheme B** specifically focuses on the **Manufacturing sector**. This scheme is designed to incentivize the hiring of **first-time employees** in manufacturing industries to boost the nation's industrial output and workforce.
 
• Under **Scheme B**, the government provides an incentive directly related to the **EPFO (Employees' Provident Fund Organisation)** contributions for both the **employee** and the **employer** during the first **four years** of employment.
 
• This initiative targets those entering the **Manufacturing sector** with a monthly salary of up to **₹1 lakh**. It is expected to benefit **30 lakh youth** entering the manufacturing workforce and their employers.
 
• The core objective of focusing on **Manufacturing** is to utilize the labor-intensive nature of the sector to absorb the growing youth population and align with the **Make in India** initiative. ***Hence, the correct answer is Manufacturing.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Scheme A - First Timers:**
 
 
• This scheme targets **first-time employees** in all **formal sectors**.
 
• It provides a **one-month wage** (up to **₹15,000**) to newly joined employees in **three installments**.
 
• The eligibility is restricted to those whose monthly salary does not exceed **₹1 lakh**, and the benefit is credited directly to the **EPFO account**.
 
 
 
• **Scheme C - Support to Employers:**
 
 
• This scheme is an **employer-centric** incentive focusing on **additional employment** across all sectors.
 
• The **Government of India** will reimburse employers up to **₹3,000 per month** for **two years** towards their **EPFO contribution** for each additional employee hired.
 
• It aims to incentivize the creation of **50 lakh** additional jobs by reducing the financial burden on **corporate entities** and **MSMEs**.
 
 
 
• **EPFO (Employees' Provident Fund Organisation):**
 
 
• The **EPFO** is a statutory body under the **Ministry of Labour and Employment**, established by the **Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952**.
 
• It serves as the primary vehicle for implementing the **ELI schemes**, as the incentives are disbursed based on **social security contributions**.

questions.question: What new title did the Amendment give to the Waqf Act, 1995?

options.text: Unified Waqf Empowerment Act and management of Waqf properties and boards, 1995
United Waqf Management, Empowerment, Efficiency and Development Act, 1995

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**United Waqf Management, Empowerment, Efficiency and Development Act, 1995**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024** was introduced in the **Lok Sabha** on **August 8, 2024**, by the **Union Minister of Minority Affairs**, **Kiren Rijiju**.
 
• One of the most significant changes proposed in the bill is the renaming of the **Waqf Act, 1995** to the **United Waqf Management, Empowerment, Efficiency and Development Act, 1995**. ***Hence, the correct answer is United Waqf Management, Empowerment, Efficiency and Development Act, 1995.***
 
• The bill seeks to amend the existing **1995 Act** to address issues related to the **powers of Waqf Boards**, registration of properties, and the overall **transparency** of the administration.
 
• The amendment aims to ensure better **management** and **efficiency** in the utilization of **Waqf properties** for the intended **charitable** and **religious** purposes.
 
• It introduces a more inclusive structure for the **Central Waqf Council** and **State Waqf Boards**, ensuring the representation of **women** and **non-Muslims** in these bodies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Waqf Properties in India:**
 
 
• A **Waqf** is a permanent dedication of **movable or immovable property** for purposes recognized by **Muslim Law** as pious, religious, or charitable.
 
• India has the **largest landholding** under Waqf in the world after the military and railways, with approximately **8.7 lakh properties** spread across **9.4 lakh acres**.
 
 
 
• **Role of the District Collector:**
 
 
• The **2024 Amendment Bill** proposes to give the **District Collector** the authority to determine whether a property is **Waqf property** or **government land**.
 
• In the previous framework, the **Waqf Board** had the power to decide the status of a property under **Section 40** of the **1995 Act**, a provision the new bill seeks to **omit**.
 
 
 
• **Inclusive Composition:**
 
 
• The bill mandates that the **Central Waqf Council** and **State Waqf Boards** must include **two women members**.
 
• It also allows for the appointment of **two non-Muslim members** to the **State Waqf Boards** to enhance administrative diversity.
 
 
 
• **Digitization and Transparency:**
 
 
• The amendment emphasizes the **mandatory registration** of Waqf properties through a **centralized portal** to prevent **encroachment** and facilitate **digitization** of records.
 
• It introduces stricter **auditing** requirements by the **Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)** or designated officers to ensure **financial accountability**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legislative History:** The original **Waqf Act** was passed in **1954**, which was later replaced by the **Waqf Act, 1995**. Significant amendments were previously made in **2013** to strengthen the **Waqf Tribunals** and the powers of the **Waqf Boards**.
 
• **Waqf-alal-aulad:** The **2024 Bill** clarifies provisions regarding **Waqf-alal-aulad** (Waqf for the benefit of the donor's family), ensuring that it does not lead to the **deprivation of inheritance rights** for legal heirs, including **women**.
 
• **Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC):** Following its introduction in **August 2024**, the bill was referred to a **Joint Parliamentary Committee** for detailed scrutiny due to concerns raised by various **stakeholders** regarding the autonomy of religious institutions.
</ul

questions.question: Where did the RBI relocate its Andhra Pradesh Regional Office in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vijayawada**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** officially relocated its **Andhra Pradesh Regional Office** to **Vijayawada** in **June 2025**.
 
• Prior to this relocation, the regional operations for **Andhra Pradesh** were primarily managed from the **Hyderabad** regional office, which had been serving as the joint hub since the state bifurcation in **2014**.
 
• The shifting of the office to **Vijayawada** is a strategic move to ensure better administrative efficiency and to bring central banking services closer to the state's administration and its residents.
 
• The **Vijayawada** office is tasked with overseeing **banking regulation**, **currency management**, and financial operations specifically tailored to the economic landscape of **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• This move aligns with the broader requirement of establishing independent state-level administrative infrastructure following the conclusion of the **10-year** joint capital agreement for **Hyderabad**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **State Bifurcation Context**:
 
 
• Under the **Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014**, the state was divided into **Telangana** and the residual state of **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• While **Amaravati** was designated as the capital, many essential services and financial regulatory bodies continued to operate from **Hyderabad** during the transition period.
 
 
 
• **Role of RBI Regional Offices**:
 
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India** operates multiple regional offices across the **country**, usually located in state capitals, to manage **monetary policy** implementation at the local level.
 
• These offices house departments such as the **Issue Department**, which manages the circulation of **banknotes** and coins, and the **Banking Department**, which acts as a banker to the **Government**.
 
 
 
• **Vijayawada's Significance**:
 
 
• **Vijayawada**, located in the **NTR district**, is considered the **commercial capital** of **Andhra Pradesh** due to its high density of trade, commerce, and logistics activities.
 
• Its central location and connectivity make it a preferred administrative choice for financial institutions like the **RBI**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Reserve Bank of India** was established on **April 1, 1935**, in accordance with the provisions of the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**.
 
• It was originally established in **Calcutta** (now **Kolkata**) but was permanently moved to **Mumbai** in **1937**.
 
• The **RBI** acts as the **lender of last resort** and is responsible for maintaining **price stability** while keeping the objective of **growth** in mind.
 
• Currently, the **RBI** has **31** regional offices and sub-offices spread across **India**, ensuring a wide-reaching **financial inclusion** and **regulatory** framework.
</ul

questions.question: In the 2025 Asian Athletics Championships held in Gumi, South Korea, Tejaswin Shankar made history by becoming the first Indian to win two medals in which specific athletics event?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Decathlon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tejaswin Shankar** created history at the **2025 Asian Athletics Championships** by clinching a **silver medal** in the **Decathlon** event.
 
• This feat made him the **first Indian athlete** to win **two medals** in the **Decathlon** discipline at the **Asian Athletics Championships**. He had previously won his first **silver medal** in the same event during the **2023** edition held in **Bangkok**, **Thailand**.
 
• The **2025** edition of the championships was hosted in **Gumi**, **South Korea**, from **May 27 to May 31, 2025**.
 
• Shankar demonstrated exceptional consistency across **ten different track and field disciplines** over two days to secure his podium finish, reinforcing his position as one of Asia's premier multi-event athletes.
 
• His transition from being a **High Jump** specialist to a successful **Decathlete** has been a significant milestone for **Indian Athletics**, showcasing versatility and endurance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tejaswin Shankar's Career Profile**: 
 
 
• He holds the **Indian National Record** in **High Jump** with a mark of **2.29 metres**, set in **April 2018**.
 
• In the **2022 Commonwealth Games** held in **Birmingham**, he won a **bronze medal** in the **High Jump**, which was India's first-ever medal in that specific discipline at the CWG.
 
• He won a **silver medal** in the **Decathlon** at the **2022 Asian Games** (held in **2023**) in **Hangzhou**, **China**, with a score of **7666 points**.
 
 
 
• **The Decathlon Event**: 
 
 
• A **Decathlon** is a combined event in athletics consisting of **ten events**. **Day 1** includes the **100m sprint**, **long jump**, **shot put**, **high jump**, and **400m run**.
 
• **Day 2** features the **110m hurdles**, **discus throw**, **pole vault**, **javelin throw**, and the **1500m run**.
 
• Performance is judged on a **points system** based on the **World Athletics** scoring tables rather than just the final position in each individual race or throw.
 
 
 
• **Asian Athletics Championships**:
 
 
• It is a biennial event organized by the **Asian Athletics Association (AAA)**. The **2025** championships in **Gumi** marked the **26th edition** of the tournament.
 
• India has historically performed well in these championships, with athletes like **Neeraj Chopra**, **Hima Das**, and **Tajinderpal Singh Toor** previously bringing home gold medals.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context**: Before **Tejaswin Shankar**, India had seen success in **Decathlon** through athletes like **Vijay Singh Chauhan**, who won **gold** at the **1974 Asian Games**, but Shankar is the first to achieve **multiple medals** at the **Asian Athletics Championships** specifically.
 
• **Global Rankings**: Shankar's performances in the **Decathlon** have propelled him into the top tier of **Asian athletes**, making him a strong contender for international qualification in multi-sport events.
 
• **Comparison with Other Events**: Unlike the **Heptathlon** (which consists of **7 events** and is the standard combined event for **women**) or the **Pentathlon** (which consists of **5 events**), the **Decathlon** is considered the ultimate test of an athlete's all-around capability.
</ul

questions.question: In 2025, the maiden flight-tests of the Integrated Air Defence Weapon System (IADWS) by Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) were conducted off the coast of which of the following states of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The maiden flight-tests of the **Integrated Air Defence Weapon System (IADWS)** were successfully conducted by the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** in **2025**.
 
• The tests were carried out off the coast of **Odisha**, specifically from the **Integrated Test Range (ITR)** located at **Chandipur**.
 
• This **IADWS** is designed to provide a **multi-layered air defence shield** for high-value assets and metropolitan areas, such as **New Delhi**, against a variety of aerial threats including **missiles**, **drones**, and **aircraft**.
 
• The flight-test in **2025** aimed to validate the **interception capabilities** of the system at various altitudes and ranges, ensuring the seamless integration of **radars**, **command and control units**, and **missile launchers**.
 
• The successful trial marks a significant milestone in India's **self-reliance (Atmanirbhar Bharat)** in advanced missile technology and urban **strategic defence**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Integrated Air Defence Weapon System (IADWS):**
 
 
• Commonly compared to the **National Advanced Surface-to-Air Missile System (NASAMS-II)**, it incorporates **advanced sensors** and **high-speed interceptors**.
 
• It is intended to work in tandem with existing systems like the **S-400 Triumf** and the **Ballistic Missile Defence (BMD)** shield to create a comprehensive safety net over **Indian airspace**.
 
 
 
• **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO):**
 
 
• **DRDO** was established in **1958** by merging the **Technical Development Establishment (TDEs)** and the **Directorate of Technical Development & Production (DTDP)**.
 
• It operates under the **Ministry of Defence**, Government of India, with its headquarters in **New Delhi**.
 
• It is responsible for the development of critical **defence technologies**, including the **Agni** and **Prithvi** series of missiles.
 
 
 
• **Integrated Test Range (ITR), Chandipur:**
 
 
• Located in the **Balasore district** of **Odisha**, it is India's premier laboratory for the **test and evaluation** of rockets and missiles.
 
• The range provides a safe environment for **long-range weapon testing** over the **Bay of Bengal**.
 
• Another key facility in **Odisha** is **Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Island** (formerly Wheeler Island), used for **strategic missile** launches.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Strategic Significance:** The deployment of **IADWS** is crucial for protecting the **National Capital Region (NCR)** from potential **aerial strikes** or **suicide drone** attacks.
 
• **Collaborative Effort:** While developed by **DRDO**, the system involves contributions from **Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL)** and other **private sector partners** for manufacturing electronic components and **radar modules**.
 
• **Modernization:** This test is part of the broader **Indian Air Force (IAF)** modernization plan to phase out legacy Soviet-era **air defence** systems with **indigenous technology**.
</ul
